title: Switch to another user's shell
summary: Use the `su` command to switch your current terminal session to another user, such as root. You will need to enter that user's password.

steps.explain: Run `su` to switch to the root user, or `su <username>` to switch to a specific user. You will be prompted for that user's password.

alternatives.explain: Switch to a specific user by name.

placeholders.name: USERNAME
placeholders.description: The name of the user you want to switch to.

alternatives.explain: Switch to a specific user and simulate a full login shell (loads their environment variables).

placeholders.name: USERNAME
placeholders.description: The name of the user you want to switch to.

rollback.explain: Type `exit` or press Ctrl+D to leave the other user's shell and return to your own.

warnings: You must know the password of the user you are switching to.
Switching to root gives you full control over the system; be careful with commands.
